examples.title: Two readings of one sentence
examples.stimulus: I saw the astronomer with the telescope.
examples.task: Identify what the prepositional phrase modifies in each reading.
examples.observation: The prepositional phrase can attach to the verb phrase or to the object noun phrase. Both trees preserve the surface word order.
examples.output:
VP attachment: I used the telescope.
NP attachment: The astronomer had the telescope.

examples.title: Add one layer of possession
examples.task: Identify the recursive phrase and add one more layer of the same type.
examples.observation: The possessor of the cat is itself a possessed noun phrase. Adding another possessor preserves the embedding pattern.
examples.output:
Mira’s neighbor’s cousin’s cat slept.
[NP [NP [NP Mira’s neighbor]’s cousin]’s cat]

examples.title: Find the position of the missing object
examples.task: Link the fronted object to its corresponding trace in the clause.
examples.observation: The interpreted object of redraw is which map. The shared index links the surface phrase to its original position.
examples.output: [CP Which mapᵢ [C did] [TP Lena [VP redraw tᵢ]]]

examples.title: Infer the voicing environment
examples.stimulus:
n a b a / n a p
s i d a / s i t
l u g a / l u k
examples.task: Infer a rule from these illustrative matched forms. Treat each row as a stem with and without a vowel suffix.
examples.observation: Voiced stops occur before the vowel suffix. Their voiceless counterparts occur at the end of the bare word.
examples.output:
Voiced stop → voiceless stop / _ #
# denotes the word boundary.
